query: How can educators improve learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: teacher_instructional_quality
per_column.rationale: Instructional quality is an intervenable lever educators can actually improve or change; a valid what-if treatment directly tied to the 'how can educators improve' framing.

per_column.name: engagement_modality
per_column.rationale: The mode of engagement (live, gamified, asynchronous, etc.) is a configurable, settable design choice educators can decide on — a second intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: peer_social_interaction_quality
per_column.rationale: Peer/community quality plausibly affects both how much active instruction/modality is deployed and student satisfaction; a common cause not named in the query. Could also be partly a mediator, but treated as a background factor here.

per_column.name: student_disengagement_pattern
per_column.rationale: Disengagement is a downstream response to instruction/modality that in turn lowers satisfaction; it lies on the causal path and is a mediator, not a confounder.

per_column.name: subject_format_fit
per_column.rationale: How well the subject suits the delivery format is a common cause: it shapes which modality/instruction is feasible and independently affects satisfaction; not named in the query (subject appears in original columns, but format-fit does not).

judge.rationale: The set includes clearly intervenable treatments (instructional quality, engagement modality) that educators can set, satisfying part (a) of the what-if claim. For part (b), two plausible confounders (subject_format_fit, peer_social_interaction_quality) are present and were NOT named in the query, demonstrating some capability. However, student_disengagement_pattern is a mediator (on the causal path from treatment to outcome), so it does not count and would introduce bias if adjusted for. Overall the intervention setup is realized moderately: valid settable treatments plus a couple of genuine, non-named confounders, but the confounder set is thin and partly ambiguous with mediation.
